📌 London – Iran’s ambassador to Germany has criticized Western governments for remaining silent over the US-Israeli military aggression against Iran, saying they are now expressing concern about the economic consequences of the same aggression for their own countries.

Majid Nili made the remarks in a message published on Sunday, in which he took aim at countries that failed to condemn the military attack on Iran but are now worried about its economic repercussions.
​
“Those who yesterday welcomed the US and Israeli regime’s aggression against Iran through their silence or irresponsible positions are today concerned about the economic consequences of that aggression for their own countries,” Nili said, according to the Persian translation of his message.
​
Referring to a German proverb, he added: “Man soll den Tag nicht vor dem Abend loben,” meaning “Do not praise the day before evening.”
​
Nili’s remarks come as the economic repercussions of the US-Israeli aggression against Iran, particularly in energy markets, are placing growing pressure on European economies.
​
According to Germany’s Federal Statistical Office, energy prices in the country rose by 12.2% in October compared with the same month last year.
​
Eurostat data showed that eurozone inflation climbed to 3.8% in September, while energy prices surged by 18.9% year-on-year, making energy the largest contributor to the bloc’s annual inflation.
​
Meanwhile, Euronews reported that the European benchmark natural gas price had surpassed 100 euros per megawatt-hour for the first time since 2022, compared with around 32 euros before the US-Israeli military aggression against Iran.
​
The military aggression against Iran has disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, one of the world’s most strategic energy transit routes, triggering widespread volatility in global energy markets and raising concerns over the security of oil and gas supplies.

🎙 86th Naval Flotilla’s voyage a historic achievement, says Iranian Navy commander

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Iranian Navy commander Rear Admiral Shahram Irani has described the 86th Naval Flotilla’s voyage as a historic achievement, saying it was the result of months of planning.

Speaking at a ceremony on Sunday, Rear Admiral Irani described the 86th Naval Flotilla’s voyage as a historic achievement for the Iranian Navy, completed despite challenging ocean conditions.
​
He said the flotilla’s presence in ports across various countries provided an opportunity to introduce Iran’s Islamic-Iranian culture and identity and demonstrate the Islamic Republic’s power.
​
Irani also highlighted faith, hope, and self-confidence as key factors enabling the Armed Forces to counter complex threats and hybrid warfare.
​
The Iranian Navy’s 86th flotilla sailed around the world, starting from the southern port city of Bandar Abbas on September 20, 2022, and cruising through the Indian Ocean, Pacific Ocean, and Atlantic Ocean before returning to the country’s shores after an eight-month voyage.
​
The flotilla sailed through 65,000 kilometers of international waters and circumnavigated the globe.
​
The objective was to expand naval presence in international waters and send a message that the Iranian Navy will not be deterred by harsh sanctions and saber-rattling, according to officials.
​
It was the first-of-its-kind, round-the-world voyage undertaken by an Iranian Navy flotilla and came amid unprecedented sanctions and economic terrorism against the Islamic Republic.
